title: Moussaka
subtitle: Greek layered aubergine and lamb with bechamel
excerpt: Layers of sliced roasted aubergine and spiced lamb mince, topped with a thick bechamel sauce and baked until golden. Greece's greatest baked dish: rich, deeply flavoured, and worth the effort.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moussaka is the signature dish of Greek cuisine. The modern layered version with bechamel was created or codified by chef Nikolaos Tselementes in the 1920s, who introduced the French-style white sauce topping. Earlier versions existed across the Balkans, Middle East, and North Africa without the bechamel. The Greek version always uses aubergine and lamb mince. The spice profile is cinnamon and allspice in the meat, which distinguishes it from Italian meat sauces.

recipeTools.notes: A deep 30 x 20 cm baking dish.
For the meat sauce and bechamel.

content.text: Roast the aubergine slices separately until golden before layering: they must be pre-cooked or they will steam in the dish and make the moussaka waterlogged. The bechamel must be thick enough to hold its shape when spread but not so thick it becomes stiff. Let the assembled dish rest for 20 minutes before cutting: it firms up and slices cleanly.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Brush the aubergine slices with 3 tablespoons of olive oil. Season. Roast on baking trays for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden. Set aside. Reduce the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4.

Heat the remaining oil in a large saucepan. Fry the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the lamb mince and cook until browned. Add the tinned tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon, and allspice. Season. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Make the bechamel: melt the butter, add the flour, cook for 1 minute. Add the milk gradually, whisking. Simmer until thick. Remove from heat. Add most of the cheese, the eggs, and nutmeg. Season.

Layer half the aubergines in the baking dish. Add the meat sauce. Top with remaining aubergines. Pour the bechamel over. Scatter with the remaining cheese. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden. Rest for 20 minutes before cutting.
